body: Hello, in your issue, you fetch this : http://localhost:3000/api/model BUT in your api folder your route is /app/api/model-name/route.js. So normally your fetch is like this : http://localhost:3000/api/model-name with GET method.

> Hello, in your issue, you fetch this : http://localhost:3000/api/model BUT in your api folder your route is /app/api/model-name/route.js. So normally your fetch is like this : http://localhost:3000/api/model-name with GET method.

You're right, the comment has te wrong notation. I edited it. This is sadly not the solution for the fix as this is an error only present in the issue documentation and not the actual code.
Why not import the route in page and directly use the GET method ? No extra round trip. Did this work before ? Does this fail when doing the same fetch at the middleware instead of page ?

> Why not import the route in page and directly use the GET method ? No extra round trip. Did this work before ? Does this fail when doing the same fetch at the middleware instead of page ?

The code in the example is a simplified scenario from the reproduction repository. The page.js is not the only location I am using this fetch (also client-side components). The reason the I am using a route handler is because I want to access API keys from my .env that I don't want to be accessible from the client-side. I've successfully done fetches to localhost:3000 in early versions of v13.

Seems like quite a common scenario to me. Either I am doing something wrong fundamentally, or there's a setting I am missing. Everythings works fine when I run `npm run dev`.
@SpinBoxx Interesting, what node version are you using? I am using node 18.18.2
Node has had issues with resolving IPv6 vs v4, maybe related? Have you tried on another OS?

I just tested the [reproduction environment](https://github.com/douwepausma/build-with-routehandlers-reproduction) with node v16, v18, v20 and still getting errors. Reading the [documentation](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/building-your-application/data-fetching/fetching-caching-and-revalidating#fetching-data-on-the-client-with-route-handlers) I assumed route handlers would work on server components, I guess they are meant for client components and actually don't work  on server components at all. Kind of annoying as I have to create two function doing to same thing for both client and server.

> Node has had issues with resolving IPv6 vs v4, maybe related? Have you tried on another OS?

I've read something about that as well. I tried locally on mac, but Vercel is giving issues as well.

Have you tried editing package.json script to

"dev": "NODE_OPTIONS='--dns-result-order=ipv4first' next dev",

Or using dns.lookup or something like that before fetching to actually see what it resolves to?
